priority: Priority 1: outdoor informal workers in Delhi-NCR
name: When the air stops work: income protection for restriction-affected workers
problem_and_population: Construction workers first, then vendors and platform workers who lose earnings when GRAP restrictions stop work; migrants and women are most often excluded
evidence_supporting_action: Restrictions and compensation duties are documented; registration gap leaves most workers out; unspent welfare cess
intervention_combination: Registration and renewal drives; payment tracking after each closure; legal support; design and pilot of income continuity for non-construction workers with a public payer; worker organising
why_philanthropy: Government pays the transfers but no one is paid to close the registration gap or measure who is missed
additionality: Builds on court orders and existing boards rather than parallel schemes
potential_partners: Construction unions; MHT; Help Delhi Breathe; Delhi BOCW board; labour department; platform social security board
geography_and_rationale: Delhi-NCR first (only place with GRAP compensation), then other NCR states bound by the same order
recurring_service_requirements: Case workers each season; board data systems (public)
expected_outcomes_and_measurement: Share of affected workers paid within 30 days; time to payment; inclusion of migrants and women; measured earnings loss vs compensation
main_uncertainties_and_failure_modes: Board refuses data access; payments delayed; extension to other trades lacks a payer
sustainability_and_adoption: Board and labour department absorb registration outreach; platform fund adopts tested design
expand_redesign_exit_conditions: Expand if paid share rises measurably in two seasons; redesign if board data unavailable; exit when board runs outreach itself

priority: Priority 1: outdoor informal workers in Delhi-NCR
name: Essential work in toxic air: occupational protection for the city's informal workforce
problem_and_population: Sanitation workers, waste pickers, security guards and delivery riders with documented high exposure and lung impairment
evidence_supporting_action: Strong problem evidence (spirometry, in-vehicle and rider exposure); entitlements exist but reach is uneven; weak evidence on PPE adherence
intervention_combination: Enrolment in existing entitlements (NAMASTE profiling, municipal ID cards, PM-JAY cover, OSH Code health check-ups); fit-tested respirator programmes with employer co-payment; shift timing away from inversion hours; periodic spirometry; organising for employer and platform duties
why_philanthropy: Schemes and employer duties now exist (NAMASTE for waste pickers from 2024-25; OSH Code from November 2025) but nobody funds enrolment, benefit tracking or tested respirator models for outdoor informal work
additionality: Fills a gap no public programme covers for informal workers
potential_partners: Municipal corporations and contractors; Chintan; waste-picker collectives; platform worker unions; NPCCHH
geography_and_rationale: Delhi (evidence base exists), then a second city
expected_outcomes_and_measurement: Personal exposure; adherence; lung function trend; costs borne by workers
main_uncertainties_and_failure_modes: Low adherence in heat; employers refuse co-payment; screening without treatment
sustainability_and_adoption: Municipal procurement standards; platform social security fund covers screening
expand_redesign_exit_conditions: Expand if adherence and exposure reduction are shown; redesign around shift timing if respirators fail
classes: A (entitlement enrolment); B (respirator programmes, shift redesign)

name: Children's air: schools and early years
problem_and_population: Children in high-exposure cities, especially in government schools and households without private protection; pregnant women as a linked group
evidence_supporting_action: School education RCT shows behaviour and some health gains; purifiers clean air but outcomes lag; closures disrupt learning
intervention_combination: Curriculum-embedded air-pollution education; redesigned classroom filtration pilots with behaviour messaging and maintenance budgets; school continuity planning to reduce closures; review of antenatal advice
why_philanthropy: Education systems will adopt proven low-cost content but rarely test hardware rigorously
additionality: Extends a tested Delhi design to state schools; tests purifiers properly before mass procurement
potential_partners: KV Sangathan; state education departments; research teams behind the KV trial; CEEW
geography_and_rationale: Delhi plus one IGP city with weaker capacity (e.g. Patna) to test transfer
infrastructure_component: Classroom HEPA units only as measured pilots
recurring_service_requirements: Teacher time; filter replacement and electricity (education department)
expected_outcomes_and_measurement: Behaviour and awareness; self-reported symptoms; spirometry; classroom PM; days of in-person schooling retained
main_uncertainties_and_failure_modes: Effects fade; purifier offsets persist; procurement races ahead of evidence
sustainability_and_adoption: Curriculum adoption by boards; purifiers only if department funds running costs
expand_redesign_exit_conditions: Expand education if second-site effects hold; stop purifier pilots if outcomes still lag education alone

priority: Not prioritised: kept in the learning agenda
name: Fair transition in production and rural energy
problem_and_population: Kiln workers (often SC/ST migrant families in debt bondage) and biomass-cooking households in rural Bihar and the IGP
evidence_supporting_action: Kiln emission savings reported; labour abuses documented; LPG cuts exposure but health effect alone limited; rural exposure high but poorly monitored
intervention_combination: Kiln conversion paired with labour standards and worker support; calibrated rural monitoring with response protocols; research on sustained clean cooking within government programmes
why_philanthropy: Owners and governments fund capital; nobody funds the worker side or the measurement
additionality: Adds labour and equity conditions to transitions already mandated
potential_partners: BSPCB; WRI India; anti-slavery organisations; IIT Kanpur; World Bank UP programme
geography_and_rationale: Bihar (major kiln hub and migrant origin; lowest monitoring)
expected_outcomes_and_measurement: Kiln emissions; worker pay records, debt, child presence; actions triggered by monitoring
main_uncertainties_and_failure_modes: Owners resist labour conditions; data disputes with regulators; long time to health outcomes
sustainability_and_adoption: State boards adopt calibration and response protocols; labour department enforces records
expand_redesign_exit_conditions: Not funded as a portfolio at this stage; its questions (G6, G7) stay in the learning agenda and can be revisited after the priority portfolios report first results
